item.title: ARMember WordPress Plugin Insecure Password Reset via Plaintext Key + SQLi Chain (CVE-2026-5076)
item.description:

CVE / Advisory CVE-2026-5076 (chained with CVE-2026-5073, CVE-2026-5074)
Category web
Severity Critical
CVSS Score 9.8 (Critical)
Status PoC
Tags wordpress, armember, membership-plugin, sql-injection, password-reset, plaintext-key, account-takeover, cwe-640
Related N/A

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System ARMember – Membership Plugin & Content Restriction (WordPress plugin)
Versions Affected Premium <= 7.3.1 (patched in 7.3.2)
Language / Platform PHP / WordPress; Python 3 exploit client (requests)
Authentication Required No (unauthenticated, chained via SQL injection)
Network Access Required Yes

Summary

ARMember Premium <= 7.3.1 stores password-reset keys (arm_reset_password_key user meta) in plaintext, and the plugin’s member-directory AJAX endpoint (arm_directory_paging_action) is vulnerable to unauthenticated SQL injection via the order parameter. The included main.py exploit chains these together: it detects ARMember, locates a member-directory page to extract the required nonce/template ID, confirms boolean/time-based blind SQLi, enumerates the WordPress table prefix and admin account, triggers a password-reset request, and then uses the same blind SQLi to directly read the plaintext reset key (or the hashed WordPress user_activation_key as a fallback) out of the database. It then submits that key to either ARMember’s or WordPress’s own reset-password endpoint to set a new admin password and verifies login, achieving full administrator account takeover without ever needing to receive the reset email.

item.title: User Registration & Membership Unauthenticated Admin Privilege Escalation (CVE-2026-1492)

Status Weaponized
Tags wordpress, privilege-escalation, unauthenticated, ajax, membership-plugin, admin-takeover, cwe-269
Related N/A

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System User Registration & Membership WordPress plugin (Custom Registration Form Builder, Login Form, User Profile, Content Restriction & Membership)
Versions Affected Up to and including 5.1.2
Language / Platform Python 3 PoC against a PHP/WordPress AJAX backend
Authentication Required No
Network Access Required Yes

Summary

The plugin’s user_registration_membership_register_member AJAX handler accepts a client-supplied role field inside the members_data JSON payload during membership registration, without enforcing a server-side allowlist or capability check. An unauthenticated attacker can chain a normal user registration request with a follow-up membership-registration AJAX call that sets "role":"administrator", silently upgrading the newly created account to full WordPress Administrator. The included PoC automates discovery of membership plan IDs and nonces, performs the registration and role-injection AJAX calls, then verifies admin access and logs working credentials, supporting multi-target, multi-threaded runs.
